Cases in state totals that no county accounts for

Source: R/no_county_cases.R
no_county_cases.Rd

A state's total in CDC AtlasPlus is usually larger than the sum of its counties. no_county_cases() compares each state total with the county counts supplied. Run it after impute_suppressed() for the remainder that no county accounts for; on county data straight from get_atlas() it reports only the gap left by published counts.

For CDC's HIV estimates (get_atlas("estimate")), county data cover only the Ending the HIV Epidemic (EHE) counties, so the remainder can include people in counties outside EHE coverage and isn't necessarily cases with no county; a message says so.

The remainder is a difference, not a count of identified cases. One likely explanation is cases whose county of residence is unknown or not released, but CDC's documentation doesn't say so; it also includes any counties left out of x. In 2022 the gap was far larger than suppressed counties could hold at 1-4 cases each, so it can't be used to fill them in. extrapolate_from_county() leaves the remainder out by default; no_county = "spread" shares it across the state's counties instead. See the "About CDC AtlasPlus data" article.

Usage

no_county_cases(x)

Arguments

x

County data from get_atlas(geography = "county"), usually after impute_suppressed().

Value

A tibble with one row per state, indicator, year and stratum:

state_fips, state

State FIPS code and name.

indicator, year, race_ethnicity, sex, age

As in x.

state_cases

The state total published by CDC.

published_cases

Sum of the published county counts in x. NA if the remainder is withheld (see no_county_withheld).

unpublished_cases

state_cases - published_cases: cases in suppressed counties together with the remainder no county accounts for. NA if withheld.

imputed_cases

Sum of the counts impute_suppressed() filled in; NA if x hasn't been imputed.

no_county_cases

unpublished_cases - imputed_cases. Can be negative if the imputed counts are too high, and is NA if x hasn't been imputed.

no_county_withheld

Why published_cases, unpublished_cases and no_county_cases are not reported: "one county row without a published count", "no CDC county rows to count unpublished counties", or NA otherwise. (Where CDC suppressed the state total, those columns are NA for that reason instead.) See the section below.

Every column computed from state_cases is NA if CDC suppressed the state total.

Details

Downloads the state data matching x (same diseases, years and stratification) from CDC AtlasPlus, and CDC's county table for x when it isn't in the cache. The remainder also includes any county without a count in x: "Data not available" rows, counties removed by filtering x, and suppressed rows impute_suppressed() couldn't estimate (marked cases_source = "not estimated"), which count as 0 imputed cases. The report has a row only for state groups (state, indicator, year and stratum) with at least one row in x: if impute_suppressed(not_available = "drop") or filtering removed every row of a group, its state total is not reported.

State strata with one county row without a published count

Where a state stratum has exactly one county row without a published count (suppressed, "Data not available", or with no count for another reason), the state total minus the published counts is that county's count plus any cases with no county. CDC's documentation doesn't say that state totals include cases with no county, so the figure could be that county's count exactly, and no_county_cases() doesn't report it.

A county counts only if neither x nor CDC's county table for x gives its count. The remainder isn't reported if one county counts, either over both tables or over the counties CDC's table lists. So a county filtered out of x, or dropped by impute_suppressed(not_available = "drop"), still counts; a county with a count in one table but not the other doesn't; and a county in only one of the tables can't make one county without a count look like none or two. CDC's table comes from the cache when x was downloaded in this session; otherwise it is downloaded. If CDC's table has no rows for a stratum, how many counties lack a count can't be known, so that stratum's remainder isn't reported either.

For such a stratum published_cases, unpublished_cases and no_county_cases are NA and no_county_withheld says why, and a message says how many strata this applies to. state_cases (CDC's published total) and imputed_cases (the modeled estimate) are still given.

States with many cases in no county row

no_county_cases() warns, once per call, when a state has more than 25% of its published state total in no county row of x: the remainder divided by the state total, with both added up over the state's strata that are in x and have a published state total, separately for each indicator and year. The percentage is of the state totals CDC published for the strata in x. It is not a share of every case in the state when x lacks a stratum (data filtered to one sex, say) or CDC published no total for one. The warning (class "cdcatlas_state_unplaced_cases") names the states with their percentages, the five largest for each indicator and year. County counts for such a state, added up or shared across smaller areas, leave those cases out and are too low by about that share for those strata. This happens when a state's county counts are largely suppressed, or when x lacks some of the state's counties; the package does not check the cause. Nothing in the report changes.

A state is assessed only where CDC published its total and x has been through impute_suppressed(). Strata with no published state total, and strata with no row in x, are left out of its share, and so are states with no cases. CDC's HIV estimates are not assessed, because their county data cover only EHE counties. A stratum where the imputed counts exceed the state total offsets one where they fall short. The 25% is fixed.

See also

impute_suppressed(), extrapolate_from_county(); the article "About CDC AtlasPlus data" on why state totals and county counts differ.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
county <- get_atlas("hiv", "county", 2022)
county <- impute_suppressed(county)
no_county_cases(county)
} # }
